x-card.description: Read queries, schemas and tables. Changes wait for approval.

account.title: Account identifier
account.description: orgname-accountname, or an account locator with its region (xy12345.eu-central-1). Not a URL: GateRook connects to <account>.snowflakecomputing.com.

privateLink.title: Private connectivity
privateLink.description: Connect to <account>.privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com: AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link or Google Private Service Connect.

user.title: User
user.description: The login name GateRook signs in as. Grant it only roles that read: Snowflake has no read-only transaction, so its roles are the boundary.

privateKey.title: Private key (PEM)
privateKey.description: An unencrypted RSA key of at least 2048 bits, PKCS#8 or PKCS#1. Its public key is the user's RSA_PUBLIC_KEY; Test connection shows its fingerprint.

token.title: Programmatic access token
token.description: A token of the user, best restricted to a role that only reads. Snowflake accepts it only from addresses a network policy of the user allows.

warehouse.title: Warehouse
warehouse.description: Runs the statements: queries over tables need one. Empty: the user's default warehouse.

role.title: Role
role.description: Use a role that can only read outside dev. Empty: the user's default role.

database.title: Database
database.description: Where names without a database resolve. Empty: the user's default namespace.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: Where names without a schema resolve; needs Database. Write names with lower case or spaces in double quotes.

tables.title: Tables
tables.description: The tables agents may use, as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE; * matches any characters, such as ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.*, and case doesn't matter. Empty: every table the role may read.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Policies set row limits and timeouts per environment.

statementTimeoutSeconds.title: Statement timeout
statementTimeoutSeconds.description: Snowflake cancels slower statements. Empty: the environment policy's statement timeout; with both, the shorter applies.
